title: Giant Centella asiatica, a novel cultivar rich in madecassoside and asiaticoside, suppresses alpha‑melanocyte‑stimulating hormone‑induced melanogenesis through MC1R binding.
authors: Seo, Jiwon; Jeong, Chanhyeok; Oh, Seung Man; Lee, Sung-Young; Park, Han Woong; Seo, Dae Bang; Yoo, Dae Sung; Sim, Woo-Jin; Lim, Tae-Gyu; Park, Jung Han Yoon; Lee, Chang Hyung; Lee, Ki Won
one_liner_zh: 该文研究积雪草提取物通过MC1R结合抑制黑色素生成，属于小分子-受体互作，与蛋白质-DNA互作及TF-DNA结合机制无关。
abstract: The present study investigated the anti‑melanogenesis effects of Giant Centella asiatica (GCA), a new cultivator of Centella asiatica (CA) cataloged by the Korea Forest Service in 2022, and compared its efficacy with that of traditional CA. GCA has a high yield per unit area and enhanced antioxidant properties. The anti‑melanogenic effects of GCA were investigated using B16F10 melanoma cells and a 3D human skin‑equivalent model. Key molecular mechanisms were elucidated through western blotting, cAMP assays and molecular docking studies. Focus was addressed on the effect of GCA on skin whitening by comparing the ability of a GCA extract to inhibit melanin production in B16F10 melanoma cells and a 3D human skin‑equivalent model to that of CA. The results showed that the GCA extracts more effectively reduced melanin production, which was attributed to their higher content of two active components, madecassoside and asiaticoside. Further investigation revealed that GCA primarily inhibited melanogenesis through the PKA‑cAMP response element‑binding (CREB)‑microphthalmia‑associated transcription factor (MITF) axis, a key regulatory pathway in melanin synthesis. Notably, the present study, to the best of our knowledge, is the first to demonstrate that madecassoside and asiaticoside, the two principal compounds in GCA, directly bound to MC1R, which contributed to the significant skin‑whitening effects. Moreover, GCA reduced melanin production in a 3D human skin‑equivalent model, showing efficacy within a complex skin environment. These results demonstrated the superior effectiveness of GCA to that of CA for skin anti‑melanogenesis, indicating its potential as a promising natural material for targeting pigmentation disorders.
abstract_zh: 本研究探讨了巨型积雪草（GCA）的抗黑色素生成作用，GCA是韩国森林厅于2022年登记的一种积雪草（CA）新品种，并将其功效与传统CA进行了比较。GCA具有单位面积产量高和抗氧化性能增强的特点。利用B16F10黑色素瘤细胞和3D人皮肤等效模型研究了GCA的抗黑色素生成作用。通过蛋白质印迹法、cAMP检测和分子对接研究阐明了关键分子机制。研究重点聚焦于GCA对皮肤美白的影响，比较了GCA提取物与CA提取物在B16F10黑色素瘤细胞和3D人皮肤等效模型中抑制黑色素生成的能力。结果表明，GCA提取物更有效地减少了黑色素生成，这归因于其含有更高含量的两种活性成分——羟基积雪草苷和积雪草苷。进一步研究发现，GCA主要通过PKA‑cAMP反应元件结合（CREB）‑小眼畸形相关转录因子（MITF）轴抑制黑色素生成，这是黑色素合成中的关键调控通路。值得注意的是，据我们所知，本研究首次证明GCA中的两种主要化合物羟基积雪草苷和积雪草苷直接结合MC1R，这有助于显著的皮肤美白效果。此外，GCA在3D人皮肤等效模型中减少了黑色素生成，在复杂皮肤环境中显示出功效。这些结果表明，GCA在皮肤抗黑色素生成方面优于CA，表明其作为针对色素沉着障碍的天然材料的潜力。
